learn.title: Whose…? and possessive pronouns
learn.html:
Whose asks who something belongs to. It goes with a noun: Whose + noun + be + this / these? Use this for singular or uncountable nouns, and these for plural nouns.

QuestionAnswer
Whose bathing suit is this?It's mine. (= It's my bathing suit.)
Whose jewelry is this?It's hers.
Whose clothes are these?They're not ours.
SubjectPossessive adjective + nounPossessive pronoun
Imy bagmine
youyour bagyours
hehis baghis
sheher baghers
weour bagours
theytheir bagtheirs

A possessive pronoun replaces the noun: it is never followed by a noun. Answers: It's + pronoun (singular) and They're + pronoun (plural).

watch.wrong: Is this bag your?
watch.right: Is this bag yours?
watch.why: Without a noun after it, use the pronoun yours.

watch.wrong: The blue car is our.
watch.right: The blue car is ours.
watch.why: Our needs a noun; ours replaces it.

watch.wrong: Whose is this keys?
watch.right: Whose keys are these?
watch.why: Whose + noun + be + these (plural).

watch.wrong: It's mine bag.
watch.right: It's my bag. / It's mine.
watch.why: Mine does not go before a noun.

learn.title: Order of adjectives
learn.html:
In English, adjectives go before the noun and in a fixed order (in Spanish they go after). They do not change in the plural.

1. Opinion2. Size3. Shape4. Color5. Origin6. Material
beautiful, nice, cute, awfulbig, small, little, largeround, square, rectangularblue, red, silverTurkish, Chinesewooden, plastic, wool, silk
  • They have a beautiful black leather cover.
  • I want those cute little round speakers.
  • She bought a nice Turkish wool rug.

We almost never use more than three adjectives together. Remember the article: a before a consonant sound, an before a vowel sound (an awful old lamp).

learn.title: one and ones to avoid repeating a noun
learn.html:
Use one (singular) and ones (plural) instead of repeating a noun that was already mentioned.

ConversationMeaning
A: I like the black cover. B: I like the blue one.one = cover
A: Those speakers are cool. B: I like the silver ones on the right.ones = speakers
  • To ask: Which one do you like? / Which ones do you like?
  • To identify: an adjective before (the blue one) or a phrase after (the ones in the middle, the one on the left).
  • Before one/ones there is almost always the. With an adjective and no article: I want a new one.

watch.wrong: These chairs are old. I want new one.
watch.right: These chairs are old. I want new ones.
watch.why: Plural: ones.

watch.wrong: I like the blue ones sofa.
watch.right: I like the blue one.
watch.why: One/ones replaces the noun; they are not written together.

watch.wrong: Which ones lamp do you like?
watch.right: Which one do you like? / Which lamp do you like?
watch.why: Which one (no noun) or Which lamp (with a noun).

watch.wrong: I prefer the red.
watch.right: I prefer the red one.
watch.why: After an adjective with the, you need one/ones.

learn.title: Polite requests: Do you mind… / Would you mind…
learn.html:
To ask for permission and to ask for a favor politely:

ToStructureExample
Ask for permission (= Can I…?)Do you mind if I + verbDo you mind if I look around?
Ask someone to do something (= Can you…?)Would you mind + verb-ingWould you mind helping me in the kitchen?

How to answer. With Can / Could: Yes. / Sure. / Go (right) ahead. / OK. / No problem.

With Do you mind / Would you mind, the question means «does it bother you?», so to accept you say No: No, go right ahead. / No, not at all. / Oh, no. No problem.

To politely decline: I'm sorry, but… and give a reason.

watch.wrong: Do you mind if I opening the window?
watch.right: Do you mind if I open the window?
watch.why: After if I, use the base verb.

watch.wrong: Would you mind to help me?
watch.right: Would you mind helping me?
watch.why: Would you mind + verb with -ing.

watch.wrong: Do you mind if I sit here? Yes, go ahead.
watch.right: Do you mind if I sit here? No, go ahead.
watch.why: With mind, answering No means «it doesn't bother me».

watch.wrong: Would you mind if you close the door?
watch.right: Would you mind closing the door?
watch.why: To ask for a favor: Would you mind + -ing.

learn.title: Ordering actions: first, next, then, as soon as, while
learn.html:
To tell a routine with more than two actions, use First, … Next, … (and) then …

First, I change my clothes. Next, I turn on some music, and then I cook dinner.

WordMeaningExample
as soon asright afterAs soon as I get home, I relax.
whileat the same time as + actionI listen to music while I'm making dinner.
whenwhenWhen the kitchen is clean, I can relax.
before / afterbefore / afterI wash my face before I go to bed. / After dinner, I do the dishes.
duringduring + nounI like to watch TV during dinner.
  • During goes with a noun; while goes with subject + verb.
  • If the sentence starts with as soon as / when / after, put a comma before the second part.

watch.wrong: While I get home, I relax.
watch.right: As soon as I get home, I relax.
watch.why: Right after = as soon as, not while.

watch.wrong: I listen to music during I cook.
watch.right: I listen to music while I cook.
watch.why: With subject + verb, use while.

watch.wrong: As soon as I will get home, I call you.
watch.right: As soon as I get home, I call you.
watch.why: After as soon as, use the simple present.

watch.wrong: First I take a shower, then I eat breakfast.
watch.right: First, I take a shower. Then I eat breakfast.
watch.why: Put a comma after First and separate the ideas.

learn.title: Expressions for the home
learn.html:
• Whose … is this / are these? — Who does … belong to?
  • It's mine. / They're theirs. — answers with a possessive pronoun.
  • Which one do you like? — The blue one on the right. — to identify something.
  • Do you mind if I…? — No, go right ahead. — to ask for and give permission.
  • Would you mind …ing? — No, not at all. / No problem. — to ask for a favor.
  • First, … Next, … Then … — to tell a routine.

reading.title: Our first apartment
reading.intro: Read Daniel's text and answer the questions.
paragraphs: Last month my girlfriend Sofia and I moved into our first apartment. It is small, but it has a bright living room and a kitchen with a big window. As soon as we arrived, we started to put our things away. Sofia keeps her books on the shelves in the living room, and I keep my music files and speakers on top of the dresser in the bedroom.

The first problem was the furniture. We wanted a beautiful round wooden table, but the one in the store was too expensive. So we bought a cheap old table from a neighbor and painted it white. Now it looks great! We also have two armchairs. The blue one is mine and the gray one is hers, but we usually sit together on the sofa.

In the evening we have a routine. First, we cook dinner together. Sofia chops the onions while I set the table. After dinner, I do the dishes because she hates the sink. Then we watch the news or a movie. Sometimes our neighbor asks, "Would you mind turning down the music?" We always say, "No, not at all," and we lower the volume. Yesterday somebody left a jacket in the hall. We don't know whose it is, so we are asking everybody in the building.

listening.title: Moving day
listening.intro: Listen to the conversation between Lena, Pablo and their neighbor. You can repeat it.

lines.text: Pablo, whose boxes are these in the hall?
The big ones are ours, but the small ones are the neighbor's. She left them here yesterday.
OK. Where do you want the armchair? The brown leather one?
Put it in the living room, next to the lamp. And the round mirror goes in the bathroom.
Which one, the silver one or the black one?
The silver one. The black one is for the bedroom.
Hi! Do you mind if I take my boxes now?
No, go right ahead. They're by the door.
Thanks. Would you mind helping me carry them to my apartment?
No problem. As soon as we finish with the sofa, we can help you.
That's very kind. Then you must come for coffee.
